data.title: File Encryption for Ransom
data.summary: The sample encrypts files matching a target extension list using a symmetric key that is itself encrypted with an operator-held asymmetric key, rendering the data unrecoverable without the operator's private key.
data.description:
The design deliberately makes brute-forcing the key infeasible: a unique symmetric key per
file or per victim is wrapped with the operator's public key, so only the matching private
key — held only by the operator — can unwrap it, regardless of how the file's own
encryption algorithm is attacked. Shadow copies, backups, and System Restore points are
frequently deleted or disabled as a preceding or concurrent step specifically to remove the
recovery paths that would otherwise make the encryption irrelevant.
data.recommendation:
* Isolate affected hosts immediately to stop encryption from spreading before recovery planning begins.
* Check for and preserve any surviving backups or shadow copies the sample did not reach or delete before further action risks losing them.
* Recover the sample's key-wrapping scheme and any per-victim key material left in memory or on disk — some families are vulnerable to key recovery if captured before deletion.
data.short_recommendation: Isolate affected hosts immediately and preserve any surviving backups before they can be reached or deleted.

mitre_techniques.procedure: Generated a unique AES key per file, encrypted file contents with it, then wrapped the key with an embedded RSA public key before deleting shadow copies.

mbc_techniques.implementation: Per-file symmetric keys were wrapped with an operator-held asymmetric key, leaving decryption infeasible without it.
